text:
Let $\vec{α}=3\hat{i}+\hat{j}$ and $\vec{β}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+3\widehat{k}$
. If $\vec{β}=\vec{β}_{1}-\vec{β_{2}}$,
where $\vec{β}_{1}$
is parallel to $\vec{α}$ and $\vec{β_{2}}$
is perpendicular
to $\vec{α}$ , then $\vec{β}_{1}\times \vec{β_{2}}$ 
is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given $\vec{α}=3\hat{i}+\hat{j}$

$\vec{β}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+3\widehat{k}$

$\vec{β}_{1}$
is parallel to $\vec{α}$

$\therefore$ $\vec{β}_{1}$ = $λ$ $\vec{α}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\vec{β}_{1}$ = $3λ\hat{i}+λ\hat{j}$

$\vec{β_{2}}$
is perpendicular
to $\vec{α}$

$\vec{β_{2}}$ . $\vec{α}$ = 0

Let $\vec{β_{2}}$ = $x\hat{i}+y\hat{j}+z\widehat{k}$

$\therefore$ ($x\hat{i}+y\hat{j}+z\widehat{k}$).($3\hat{i}+\hat{j}$) = 0

$\Rightarrow$ 3x + y = 0

$\Rightarrow$ y = -3x

$\therefore$ $\vec{β_{2}}$ = $x\hat{i}-3x\hat{j}+z\widehat{k}$

Given $\vec{β}=\vec{β}_{1}-\vec{β_{2}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $(2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+3\widehat{k}$) = ($3λ\hat{i}+λ\hat{j}$) - ($x\hat{i}-3x\hat{j}+z\widehat{k}$)

= $(3λ-x)\hat{i}+(λ+3x)\hat{j}-z\widehat{k}$

$\therefore$ 3$λ$ - x = 2 ...(1)

$λ$ + 3x = -1.....(2)

z = -3

Solving (1) and (2), we get

$λ$ = $\frac{1}{2}$ and x = $-\frac{1}{2}$

$\therefore$ $\vec{β}_{1}$ = $\frac{3}{2}\hat{i}+\frac{1}{2}\hat{j}$

and $\vec{β_{2}}$ = $-\frac{1}{2}\hat{i}+\frac{3}{2}\hat{j}-3\widehat{k}$

$\vec{β}_{1}\times \vec{β}_{2}=\left |\begin{array}{lll} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \widehat{k} \\ \frac{3}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ -\frac{1}{2} & \frac{3}{2} & -3 \end{array}\right |$

= $\frac{1}{2}$($-3\hat{i}+9\hat{j}+5\widehat{k}$)
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Morning Slot

text: The value of $\int\limits _{0}^{π/2}\frac{\sin ^{3}x}{\sin x+\cos x}dx$ is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
I = $\int\limits _{0}^{π/2}\frac{\sin ^{3}x}{\sin x+\cos x}dx$ .....(1)

$\Rightarrow$ I = $\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{2}}\frac{\cos ^{3}x}{\sin x+\cos x}dx$ ......(2)

Adding those two

2I = $\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{2}}\frac{\sin ^{3}x+\cos ^{3}x}{\sin x+\cos x}dx$

= $\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{2}}\frac{(\sin x+\cos x)\left (\sin ^{2}x+\cos ^{2}x-\sin x\cos x\right )}{\sin x+\cos x}dx$

= $\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{2}}\left (\sin ^{2}x+\cos ^{2}x-\sin x\cos x\right )dx$

= $\int\limits _{0}^{\frac{π}{2}}\left (1-\frac{\sin 2x}{2}\right )dx$

= $\left [x+\frac{\cos 2x}{4}\right ]_{0}^{\frac{π}{2}}$

= $\left (\frac{π}{2}-\frac{1}{4}\right )-\left (\frac{1}{4}\right )$

$\therefore$ 2I = $\left (\frac{π}{2}-\frac{1}{2}\right )$

$\therefore$ I = $\frac{π-1}{4}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Morning Slot

text:
If ƒ(x) is a non-zero polynomial of degree four,
having local extreme points at x = –1, 0, 1; then
the set 

S = {x $\in$ R : ƒ(x) = ƒ(0)}

Contains exactly :
options: two irrational and one rational number.
two irrational and two rational numbes.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Local extreme points of f(x) is at x = –1, 0, 1.

$\therefore$ f'(x) = 0 has three solutions x = –1, 0, 1.

$\therefore$ f'(x) = k(x + 1)x(x - 1)

$\int f^{'}(x)dx=\int k(x+1)x(x-1)dx$

f(x) = $k\left [\frac{x^{4}}{4}-\frac{x^{2}}{2}\right ]+C$

Also given that

ƒ(x) = ƒ(0)

$\therefore$ $k\left [\frac{x^{4}}{4}-\frac{x^{2}}{2}\right ]+C$ = C

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{x^{2}}{2}\left (\frac{x^{2}}{2}-1\right )$ = 0

$\Rightarrow$ x = 0, $-\sqrt{2}$, $\sqrt{2}$

$\therefore$ x has two irrational and one rational value.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Morning Slot

text:
Let ƒ(x) = 15 – |x – 10|; x $\in$ R. Then the set
of all values of x, at which the function,
g(x) = ƒ(ƒ(x)) is not differentiable, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
ƒ(x) = 15 – |x – 10|

g(x) = ƒ(ƒ(x)) = 15 – |ƒ(x) – 10|

= 15 – |15 – |x – 10| – 10|

= 15 – |5 – |x – 10||

As this is a linear expression so it is non differentiable when value inside the modulus is zero.

So non differentiable when

x – 10 = 0 $\Rightarrow$ x = 10

and 5 – |x – 10| = 0

$\Rightarrow$ |x – 10| = 5

$\Rightarrow$ x - 10 = $\pm$ 5

$\Rightarrow$ x = 5, 15

$\therefore$ g(x) is not differentiable at x = 5, 10, 15.

text:
Let p, q $\in$ R. If 2 - $\sqrt{3}$ is a root of the quadratic
equation, $x^{2} + px + q = 0$, then :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
If a quadratic equation with rational coefficient has one irrational root then other root will be the conjugate of the irrational root.

Here $x^{2} + px + q = 0$ has one root 2 - $\sqrt{3}$.

$\therefore$ Other root will be 2 + $\sqrt{3}$.

Sum of the roots = -p = 4

and product of the roots = q = 1

You can see $p^{2} – 4q – 12 = 0$ satisfy value of p = -4 and q = 1.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Morning Slot

text:
Slope of a line passing through P(2, 3) and
intersecting the line, x + y = 7 at a distance of
4 units from P, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)
tags: straight lines and pair of straight lines

solution.body:
[IMG]


We know parametric form of straight line is

$\frac{x-x_{1}}{\cos θ}=\frac{y-y_{1}}{\sin θ}=r$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{x-2}{\cos θ}=\frac{y-3}{\sin θ}=4$

$\therefore$ x = 2 + 4cos$θ$

y = 3 + 4sin$θ$

$\therefore$ Point A = (2 + 4cos$θ$, 3 + 4sin$θ$)

Point A lies on line x + y = 7,

$\therefore$ (2 + 4cos$θ$) + (3 + 4sin$θ$) = 7

$\Rightarrow$ sin$θ$ + cos$θ$ = $\frac{1}{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\sin ^{2}θ+\cos ^{2}θ$ + 2sin$θ$cos$θ$ = $\frac{1}{4}$

$\Rightarrow$ 1 + sin 2$θ$ = $\frac{1}{4}$

$\Rightarrow$ sin 2$θ$ = $-\frac{3}{4}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{2\tan θ}{1+\tan ^{2}θ}$ = $-\frac{3}{4}$

$\Rightarrow$ $3\tan ^{2}θ$ + 8tan$θ$ + 3 = 0

$\Rightarrow$ tan$θ$ = $\frac{-8\pm 2\sqrt{7}}{6}$

So slope = $\frac{-8\pm 2\sqrt{7}}{6}$

By checking each options,

Slope = $\frac{1-\sqrt{7}}{1+\sqrt{7}}$

As $\frac{1-\sqrt{7}}{1+\sqrt{7}}$ = $\frac{\left (1-\sqrt{7}\right )^{2}}{1-7}$ = $\frac{8-2\sqrt{7}}{-6}$ = $\frac{-8+2\sqrt{7}}{6}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Morning Slot

 (x > 0) is $20 × 8^{7}$, then a value of
x is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\left (\frac{2}{x}+x^{\log _{8}x}\right )^{6}$

Given $T_{4} = 20 × 8^{7}$

$\Rightarrow$ ${}^{6}C_{3}\left (\frac{2}{x}\right )^{3}\left (x^{\log _{8}x}\right )^{3}$ $= 20 × 8^{7}$

$\Rightarrow$ 20$\times\frac{8}{x^{3}}\times x^{3\log _{8}x}$ $= 20 × 8^{7}$

$\Rightarrow$ $x^{3\log _{8}x-3}$ $= 8^{6}$

Taking $\log _{8}$ both side

$\Rightarrow$ ($3\log _{8}x-3$) $\times$ $\log _{8}x$ = 6

$\Rightarrow$ $3(\log _{8}x)^{2}$ - 3$\log _{8}x$ = 6

$\Rightarrow$ $(\log _{8}x)^{2}$ - $\log _{8}x$ = 2

$\Rightarrow$ ($\log _{8}x$ - 2)($\log _{8}x$ + 1) = 0

$\Rightarrow$ $\log _{8}x$ = 2 or $\log _{8}x$ = -1

$\Rightarrow$ $x = 8^{2}$ or x = $\frac{1}{8}$

 1 = $\frac{1}{4}+C$

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$α$ and $β$ are the roots of the equation
$x^{2} + x + 1 = 0$.

$\therefore$ $α$ = $ω$ and $β$ = $ω^{2}$

$\left |\begin{array}{lll} y+1 & α & β \\ α & y+β & 1 \\ β & 1 & y+α \end{array}\right |$

$C_{1}$ $\to$ $C_{1} + C_{2} + C_{3}$

= $\left |\begin{array}{lll} y+1+ω+ω^{2} & ω & ω^{2} \\ y+1+ω+ω^{2} & y+ω^{2} & 1 \\ y+1+ω+ω^{2} & 1 & y+ω \end{array}\right |$

= $\left |\begin{array}{lll} y & ω & ω^{2} \\ y & y+ω^{2} & 1 \\ y & 1 & y+ω \end{array}\right |$

As $1+ω+ω^{2}$ = 0

= $y\left |\begin{array}{lll} 1 & ω & ω^{2} \\ 1 & y+ω^{2} & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & y+ω \end{array}\right |$

$R_{2}$ $\to$ $R_{2} - R_{1}$

$R_{3}$ $\to$ $R_{3} - R_{1}$

= $y\left |\begin{array}{lll} 1 & ω & ω^{2} \\ 0 & y+ω^{2}-ω & 1-ω^{2} \\ 0 & 1-ω & y+ω-ω^{2} \end{array}\right |$

= y$\left [\left (y+ω^{2}-ω\right )\left (y+ω-ω^{2}\right )-\left (1-ω^{2}\right )(1-ω)\right ]$

$= y(y^{2}) = y^{3}$

text:
Four persons can hit a target correctly with
probabilities
$\frac{1}{2}$, $\frac{1}{3}$, $\frac{1}{4}$ and
$\frac{1}{8}$ respectively. If all hit
at the target independently, then the probability that
the target would be hit, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let four persons are A, B, C and D.

Probability of hitting a target by them,

P(A) = $\frac{1}{2}$

P(B) = $\frac{1}{3}$

P(C) = $\frac{1}{4}$

P(D) = $\frac{1}{8}$

Probability of hitting target at least once = 1 - Probability of not hitting by anybody

P(Hit) = 1 - $P\left (A–\cap B–\cap C–\cap D–\right )$

= 1 - $P\left (A–\right ).P\left (B–\right ).P\left (C–\right ).P\left (D–\right )$

= 1 - $\frac{1}{2}.\frac{2}{3}.\frac{3}{4}.\frac{7}{8}$

= $\frac{25}{32}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Morning Slot

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{n(n-1)}{2}$ = 78

$\therefore$ The inverse of  $\left [\begin{array}{ll} 1 & 13 \\ 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ]$ = $\left [\begin{array}{ll} 1 & -13 \\ 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ]$

text:
If one end of a focal chord of the parabola,
$y^{2} = 16x$ is at (1, 4), then the length of this focal
chord is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


For this parabola $y^{2} = 16x$,

a = 4

Here PQ is focal cord.

Let $P(at_{1}^{2}, 2at_{1})$ and $Q(at_{2}^{2}, 2at_{2})$.

Given P(1, 4),

$\therefore$ $at_{1}^{2} = 1$

$\Rightarrow$ $4t_{1}^{2} = 1$

$\Rightarrow$ $t_{1}^{2} =$ $\frac{1}{4}$

$\Rightarrow$ $t_{1} =$ $\frac{1}{2}$

In parabola if the parameter of one end point of the focal cord is $t_{1}$ then parameter of the other end point $t_{2} =$ $-\frac{1}{t_{1}}$

Here parameter for point $Q t_{2} = - 2$

$\therefore$ Length of focal cord 

|PQ| = a$(t_{1}-t_{2})^{2}$ = 4$\left (\frac{1}{2}+2\right )^{2}$ = 25

If the function ƒ : R – {1, –1} $\to$ A defined by 

ƒ(x) = $\frac{x^{2}}{1-x^{2}}$ , is surjective, then A is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let ƒ(x) = $\frac{x^{2}}{1-x^{2}}$ = y

$\Rightarrow$ $y\left (1-x^{2}\right )=x^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $x^{2}=\frac{y}{1+y}$

As $x^{2}$ is always $\geq$ 0.

$\therefore$ $\frac{y}{1+y}$ $\geq$ 0

 y $\in$ $(-\infty ,-1)\cup [0,\infty )$

For surjective function co-domain = Range

$\therefore$ A is R – [–1, 0).
